title: Néron lft-model existence for split-torus extensions
statement: Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain, $E=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G,H$ be smooth separated commutative finite-type $E$-group schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $G$ is geometrically connected (connected after every field extension [def-weil-connected-scheme]). Suppose $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,E})^r\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{q}H\to1$ is exact as fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site], with $r\geq0$ and $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}E[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-sc-gm-ga]; exact means $i$ identifies the scheme-theoretic kernel of $q$ and $q$ is fppf-locally surjective. Suppose every $E$-group homomorphism $H\to\mathbf G_m$ is zero. If $H$ has a Néron lft-model over $S$, then $G$ has a smooth separated commutative Néron lft-model over $S$. A Dedekind domain here means a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. A commutative group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the commutative group diagrams. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a domain $D$ with fraction field $E$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$, a Néron lft-model of a smooth $E$-group $V$ means a smooth separated $S$-group $\mathcal V$, with an $E$-group isomorphism $\mathcal V_E\simeq V$ [def-pc-base-change], for which restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,V)$ for every smooth $S$-scheme $X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Locally of finite type means that each affine source chart over an affine base chart has a finitely generated coordinate algebra [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7, printed pp.292–293 (PDF pages 298–299), construction by primitive line bundles and translated charts Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal H$ be the given Néron lft-model of $H$. The fppf-local lifting in the exact sequence makes $q$ surjective after every field extension: a lift over a nonempty covering scheme supplies a point above each point of $H$. Hence $H$ is geometrically connected, as the continuous image of the geometrically connected $G$. The group $\mathcal H$ is commutative: $\mathcal H\times_S\mathcal H$ is a smooth $S$-scheme (base change and composite of smooth maps), and the two morphisms $m$ and $m\circ\mathrm{swap}$ from it to $\mathcal H$ have equal generic restrictions because $H$ is commutative, so they agree by injectivity of the Néron restriction bijection; hence its open subgroups and their localizations are commutative too. Apply [lem-sfb-neron-neutral-local-properties] to obtain the smooth separated finite-type open subgroup $Q=\mathcal H^0$, with geometrically connected fibres and $Q_E=H$; its formation and the Néron mapping property commute with the localizations used below.

source.place: BLR 10.1, paragraph following Definition 1 and opening of Proposition 7 proof

proof.text: For each coordinate character $\chi_j:(\mathbf G_m)^r\to\mathbf G_m$, apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-character-pushout]. It gives a commutative extension $E_j\to H$ and an equivariant frame presentation $E_j=L_j^\times$. The identity gives a frame $u_j$ at $e$. In local frames of $L_j$ over both factors and over their product, multiplication in $E_j$ is $(v,w)\mapsto c(x,y)vw$, with $c$ a regular unit: equivariance under the two scalar actions forces this expression. Thus the local formulas glue to $\mu_j:p_1^*L_j\otimes p_2^*L_j\simeq m_H^*L_j$. Associativity, commutativity and the unit law are precisely the corresponding identities for multiplication in $E_j$, checked in these frames. The homomorphisms $g\mapsto[g,1]$ give $G\to\prod_HE_j$. This is an isomorphism of fppf sheaves: after locally choosing a lift $g$ of a section of $H$, it is the coordinate isomorphism $(\mathbf G_m)^r\to\prod_j\mathbf G_m$, since $[g\,i(t),1]=[g,\chi_j(t)]$. The inverse is independent of the chosen lift and glues by the sheaf condition. Representability identifies it with a group-scheme isomorphism. For $r=0$, the same argument gives $G=H$.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7 proof, printed p.292: primitive-line description; explicit coordinate-pushout realization

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-line-dedekind-extension] to $Q$ and the data $(L_j,u_j,\mu_j)$ from step 2. Its hypotheses hold by step 1. Obtain the extended lines and their frame product $B$, a smooth separated commutative finite-type $S$-group with geometrically connected fibres and exact sequence $1\to\mathbf G_{m,S}^r\to B\to Q\to1$. The specified generic extensions of the line data and the isomorphism of step 2 identify $B_E$ with the original $G$ as an extension of $H$.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7 proof, printed p.292: extend the primitive lines and form the integral connected group

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $D$. By [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr], $R=D_{\mathfrak m}$ is a DVR. By [lem-sfb-neron-neutral-local-properties], $\mathcal H_R$ is the Néron lft-model of $H$ over $R$ and $Q_R=(\mathcal H_R)^0$. It is commutative by step 1. The localization of the extension constructed in step 3 supplies the integral extension required by [lem-sfb-split-torus-translate-hull]; the hypothesis on characters is exactly the given $\operatorname{Hom}_{E\text{-grp}}(H,\mathbf G_m)=0$. Its translated-chart construction gives a smooth separated commutative lft $R$-group $N_{\mathfrak m}$ with generic fibre $G$, open identity subgroup $B_R$, and surjectivity of integral-to-generic points for every essentially smooth local DVR extension. Separation and descent are conclusions of that cited construction, not inferences merely from gluing along generic fibres.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7 proof, printed pp.292–293: local translated charts and descent

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-neron-dvr-point-criterion] to each $N_{\mathfrak m}$. Step 4 supplies smoothness, separation and every DVR-point surjectivity demanded by criterion (ii). Therefore restriction from every smooth $R$-scheme is bijective: $N_{\mathfrak m}$ is a Néron lft-model of $G$. This uses all essentially smooth DVR extensions, rather than only étale integral points.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 2, invoked in Proposition 7 proof, printed p.293

proof.text: The models $N_{\mathfrak m}$ now exist for every maximal ideal and their identity components are $B_{D_{\mathfrak m}}$ through the generic identification of step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-neron-connected-model-globalization] with this common connected finite-type model $B$. It gives a smooth separated commutative Néron lft-model $N$ over $S$ of the original $G$, with the full mapping property for all smooth $S$-schemes. No quasi-compactness assertion about $N$, or finiteness of its component groups, is needed.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7 proof, final paragraph, printed p.293; Proposition 9 (b) to (a), printed pp.294–295

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q122-323a94c37 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all five new nodes in full, plus the cited nodes (lem-sfb-split-torus-character-pushout, lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr) and the existing Néron nodes. BLR §10.1 is not in literature/ (recorded as WANTED, proof marked by: agent), so I checked each statement mathematically against my knowledge of BLR §10.1. (1) The line extension holds: Q is regular and integral, so L extends; a twist by e^*𝓛 fixes the frame; the divisor of μ is vertical and the unit law forces it to vanish; the identities hold by density. (2) The neutral component is open and of finite type (U·U argument), and localization keeps the Néron property. (3) The translated-chart hull is separated for every DVR A, since G(K^sh)∩B(A)=B(R^sh) using Q-specialisation and torus-torsor triviality. DVR-point surjectivity holds for essentially smooth A (ramification 1, Hilbert 90, π^n absorbed). (4) The DVR criterion (i)⇒(ii) holds by removing the closure of the indeterminacy locus. (5) Globalization is BLR 10.1/9. No duplicate, restatement or relabelling; all citations are in the unit (the Dedekind-localization leaf is a Mathlib tool). Not a re-split order. Batch 5: the pushout node reaches lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc, which is the generic fact that fppf coverings are fpqc. It is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so it is accepted. Two faults fixed: (a) commutativity of the Néron lft-model 𝓗, needed by the line node in step 3 and the hull node in step 4, was never established; added to step 1 via the Néron bijection on 𝓗×_S𝓗 (m vs m∘swap), referenced in step 4. (b) B3: 'geometrically connected (fibres)' had no definition in four new nodes and no citation in the item; added an inline definition citing def-weil-connected-scheme, with stmt_deps updated.
